narrative: Fire and climate dominate this issue cycle, with work on how increasing fire severity reshapes dry conifer forest diversity, how pyrodiversity relates to phylogenetic structure in post-fire communities, and whether subsurface nitrogen fuels recovery. Climate studies show Himalayan birch recruitment limits beyond the treeline, deep water use sustaining tree growth through drought, and Swedish tundra productivity rising independently of warm-adapted plants. In animal ecology, predation risk alters nut caching and so tree establishment, sympatric owls adjust vocal and diel activity, and a connectivity framework links movement trajectories to step selection. Invasion papers highlight enemy release helping an invasive grass over a native reed in salt marshes and the role of landscape configuration in alien plant spread. Conservation coverage includes the global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity, genomic erosion in a bird hotspot, and coral community change. Methods contributions include an active learning approach for camera trap images and new R packages for body size and camera trap analysis.
